ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r7.claim: The passage depicts cosmic upheaval and the collapse of social bonds; each person would offer even close family and tribe as ransom, while Hell burns and seizes those who evaded the call and hoarded wealth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r7.anchor: The flames of Hell shall tear and burn his skin

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p268/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p268/r2.speaker: ثعلب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p268/r2.claim: He defines al-fasila as a person's closest forebears.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p268/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p268/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p268/r3.claim: He defines al-fasila as a clan; another view takes it as one's closest relatives.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p268/r3.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: الفخذ. وقيل: عشيرته الأقربون.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p273/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p273/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p273/r9.claim: Al-mujrim primarily means disbeliever but can include a sinful believer under punishment; sahibah is wife, and fasila is close kin who support a person.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p273/r9.anchor: يود المجرم: أي الكافر، وقد يندرج فيه المؤمن العاصي الذي يعذب.

NAHHAS:v5p29/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p29/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p29/r11.claim: The plural forms of faṣīlah are faṣāʾil, faṣl, and faṣalān.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366#3/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366#3/r11.claim: فصيلة here means a man's closest kin, such as Banu Hashim in relation to the Prophet; Arabic can also use it for wife, but الصاحبة already names the wife here.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366#3/r11.anchor: والفصيلة في هذه الآية قرابة الرجل الأدنون، مثال ذلك بنو هاشم مع النبي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366#3/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366#3/r13.speaker: الزهري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366#3/r13.claim: Al-Zuhri reads تؤويه and تنجيه with nominative hāʾ endings.

ELMALILI:70:8-35/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:70:8-35/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:70:8-35/r5.claim: Faṣīla means the people, tribe, clan, or community that raised, sheltered, and embraced a person when in need.
ELMALILI:70:8-35/r5.anchor: içlerinde yetiştiği ve başı sıkıldığı zaman kendisini kucaklayan, barındıran kavm ü kabilesini

QUSHAYRI:v3p350/r19.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p350/r19.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p350/r19.claim: People recognize their relatives, but recognition does not soften one person's heart toward another.
QUSHAYRI:v3p350/r19.anchor: أي يعرفون أقاربهم ، ولكن لا ترق قلوب بعضهم على بعض

QUSHAYRI:v3p350/r20.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p350/r20.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p350/r20.claim: The criminal longs to ransom himself from Hell with his dearest kin and intimates, his children and family, and everyone on earth.
QUSHAYRI:v3p350/r20.anchor: ويتمنى المجرم يومئذ أن يفتدى من عذاب جهنم بأعز من كان عليه في الدنيا من قريب ونسيب وحميم وولد

FARRA:v3p183#2/r10.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p183#2/r10.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p183#2/r10.claim: Faṣīla means a person’s closest forefathers, to whom he traces his lineage.
FARRA:v3p183#2/r10.anchor: هي أصغر آبائه الذي إليه ينتمي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p612/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p612/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p612/r17.claim: Faṣīla is a person’s nearest clan, the relatives from whom he is separated.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p612/r17.anchor: { وفصيلته } عشيرته الأدنون الذين فصل عنهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p612/r18.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p612/r18.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p612/r18.claim: The verb tuwīhi means that one’s clan gathers him through kinship or shelters him in times of hardship.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p612/r18.anchor: { تويه } تضمه انتماء إليها ، أو لياذا بها في النوائب

RAZI-FULL:v30p112/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p112/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p112/r1.claim: A man’s faṣīla is his nearest kin; the term evokes separation, as a child is separated from the parents from whom he descends.
RAZI-FULL:v30p112/r1.anchor: فصيلة الرجل ، أقاربه الأقربون الذين فصل عنهم وينتهي إليهم ، لأن المراد من الفصيلة المفصولة

RAZI-FULL:v30p112/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p112/r2.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v30p112/r2.claim: The Prophet said that Fāṭima is a part of him; Rāzī uses this to illustrate the language of separation and kinship.
RAZI-FULL:v30p112/r2.anchor: قال عليه السلام : ( فاطمة بضعة مني )

RAZI-FULL:v30p112/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p112/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p112/r3.claim: Al-ʿAbbās was called the Prophet’s faṣīla because a paternal uncle stands in the place of a father.
RAZI-FULL:v30p112/r3.anchor: وكان يقال للعباس : فصيلة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ، لأن العم قائم مقام الأب

RAZI-FULL:v30p112/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p112/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p112/r4.claim: The kin may shelter him through affiliation by lineage or through his reliance on them in adversity.
RAZI-FULL:v30p112/r4.anchor: وأما قوله : { تويه } فالمعنى تضمه انتماء إليها في النسب أو تمسكا بها في النوائب

STUDYQURAN:70:12/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:70:12/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:70:12/r1.claim: The guilty, or those who work evil in 39:47, seek to ransom themselves; other verses say neither earthfuls of gold nor all earthly possessions would be accepted.
STUDYQURAN:70:12/r1.anchor: That the guilty, or elsewhere those who work evil (39:47), will seekto ransom themselves on the Day of Judgment

STUDYQURAN:70:12/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:70:12/r2.speaker: IK, Ṭ; IK, Q
STUDYQURAN:70:12/r2.claim: Faṣīlah, “kin,” may mean one’s tribe or, more specifically, one’s mother.
STUDYQURAN:70:12/r2.anchor: one’s tribe (IK, Ṭ) or more specifically one’s mother (IK, Q)

TABATABAI:70:11-18/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:11-18/r7.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:70:11-18/r7.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines faṣīla as a group separated from the tribe through a more specific shared forefather.
TABATABAI:70:11-18/r7.anchor: وقال الفصيلة الجماعة المنقطعة عن جملة القبيلة برجوعها إلى أبوة خاصة عن أبوة عامة

TABATABAI:70:11-18/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:11-18/r8.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:70:11-18/r8.claim: Others explain faṣīla as his nearest kin, separated from him like close forefathers.
TABATABAI:70:11-18/r8.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن الفصيلة عشيرته الأقربين الذين فصل عنهم كالآباء الأدنين

TABATABAI:70:11-18/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:11-18/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:70:11-18/r9.claim: The passage escalates beyond intimates not asking after one another: the criminal would ransom himself with increasingly precious relatives, then everyone on earth, if that could save him.
TABATABAI:70:11-18/r9.anchor: وسياق هذه الآيات سياق الإضراب والترقي بالنسبة إلى قوله { ولا يسأل حميم حميما } فيفيد

TABATABAI:70:11-18/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:11-18/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:70:11-18/r10.claim: The criminal is anyone implicated in crime, not only a disbeliever; he would ransom himself with his sons, beloved above all, his comforting wife, supportive brother, close kin who shelter him, then all rational beings on earth, to be saved.
TABATABAI:70:11-18/r10.anchor: والمعنى { يود } ويتمنى { المجرم } وهو المتلبس بالإجرام أعم من الكافر

TABATABAI:70:11-18/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:11-18/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:70:11-18/r13.claim: Here faṣīla is his close clan, which takes him in and embraces him.
TABATABAI:70:11-18/r13.anchor: { وفصيلته } من عشيرته الأقربين { التي تؤويه } وتضمه إليها

BURSEVI:v10p122/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p122/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p122/r1.claim: Fasila originally means a piece separated from a body; it can denote close forebears or children, since a child is separated from its parents and they from it.
BURSEVI:v10p122/r1.anchor: وهي في الأصل القطعة المفصولة من الجسد وتطلق على الآباء الأقربين وعلى الأولاد

BURSEVI:v10p122/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p122/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p122/r2.claim: Here fasila means the nearest forebears and clan, as confirmed by the preceding mention of his children.
BURSEVI:v10p122/r2.anchor: والمراد بالفصيلة في الآية هو الآباء الأقربون والعشيرة الأدنون لقوله وبنيه

BURSEVI:v10p122/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p122/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p122/r3.claim: To shelter someone is to draw them near or gather them in; his kin either include him by lineage or shelter him in adversity.
BURSEVI:v10p122/r3.anchor: أوى إلى كذا انضم إليه وآواه غيره كما قال تعالى آوى إليه أخاه

BURSEVI:v10p122/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p122/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p122/r7.claim: The soul stained by the lower self would ransom itself from separation and veiling with heart's children and qualities, its companion self, secret's brother, followers, and all spiritual and bodily powers; ruined readiness and lost time make this futile.
BURSEVI:v10p122/r7.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى مجرم الروح المنصبغ بصبغة النفس فإنه يود أن يفتدى

TABRISI:70:15-16/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:70:15-16/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:70:15-16/r14.claim: Iftidāʾ means escaping harm by offering something in its place.
TABRISI:70:15-16/r14.anchor: والافتداء افتداء الضرر عن الشيء ببدل منه

TABRISI:70:15-16/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:70:15-16/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:70:15-16/r15.claim: A faṣīlah is a branch group within a tribe, linked by a nearer ancestor beneath the broader ancestral line.
TABRISI:70:15-16/r15.anchor: والفصيلة الجماعة المنقطعة عن جملة القبيلة برجوعها إلى أبوة خاصة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r2.claim: A man’s faṣīla is his closest kin group.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r3.speaker: أبو عبيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r3.claim: Abu ʿUbayd notes that al-ʿAbbas was called the Prophet’s faṣīla.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r4.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r4.claim: Al-Layth defines faṣīla as a man’s clan branch, the group from which he comes.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r5.claim: Abu ʿUbayda and al-Mubarrad say a faṣīla is narrower and closer in lineage than a tribe.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r5.anchor: الفصيلة دون القبيلة في النسب، أي أقرب وأخص من القبيلة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r6.speaker: رؤبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r6.claim: Ruʾba’s line uses faṣāʾil for subdivisions of people and is cited as evidence for the lineage sense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r6.anchor: وقال رؤبة: والناس إن فصلتهم فصائلا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r7.speaker: أبو العباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r7.claim: Abu al-ʿAbbas says a faṣīla is a piece of the body and is below a tribe in rank; a man’s kin are named by analogy as part of him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r7.anchor: وقال أبو العباس: الفصيلة: القطعة من أعضاء الجسد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the faṣīla as a man’s clan and relatives to whom he belongs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد عشيرته وأقاربه التي ينتهي إليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r9.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r9.claim: Muqatil says it is his nearest clan branch, the people who shelter him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r9.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يعني فخذه الأدنى يأوي إليهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r10.claim: The criminal hopes to ransom himself with these people and possessions, but no ransom, even of everything, will save him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r10.anchor: يقول الله تعالى: {يود المجرم لو يفتدي} بهذه الأشياء {ثم ينجيه} ذلك الفداء. {كلا} لا ينجيه ذلك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:70:8-13/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:70:8-13/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:70:8-13/r8.claim: His “faṣīla” is the clan from which he separated, which shelters him through kinship.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:70:8-13/r8.anchor: { وفصيلته } عشيرته التي فصل منها { التي تؤويه } تضمه إليها في النسب.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r3.claim: The sinner's psychological terror is so intense that he would sacrifice his spouse, children, closest relatives and loved ones, and even everyone on earth.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r3.anchor: insanın âkıbetinden sarsıcı bir kesit verilmektedir. Buna rağmen o gün suçlu kişinin, en değerli varlıkları olan eşini, çocuklarını ve diğer yakınlarını

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r4.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r4.claim: Exegetes say the “sinner” whose state is described can mean unbelievers or, more generally, sinners.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r4.anchor: Müfessirler, burada ruh hali tasvir edilen “mücrim”in (suçlu) inkârcıları veya daha genel olarak günahkârları ifade ettiğini belirtirler

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p485#8/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p485#8/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p485#8/r1.claim: Faṣīla means a person’s closest clan or family group.

MAJAZ:v2p269/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p269/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p269/r3.claim: Faṣīla is a smaller group than a tribe, a clan or sub-clan that shelters its members; the sequence runs from broad shaʿb through tribes to faṣīla.
MAJAZ:v2p269/r3.anchor: «وفصيلته التي تؤويه» (13) دون القبيلة، الشعوب أكثر من القبائل ثم الفصيلة، فخذه التى تؤويه ..

SAMIN-DURR:70:13-14/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:70:13-14/r1.speaker: ثعلب
SAMIN-DURR:70:13-14/r1.claim: Thaʿlab defines فصيلة as a person's nearest forefathers.

SAMIN-DURR:70:13-14/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:70:13-14/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
SAMIN-DURR:70:13-14/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda defines فصيلة as the clan or tribal subdivision.

SAMIN-DURR:70:13-14/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:70:13-14/r3.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:70:13-14/r3.claim: Another explanation is that فصيلة means one's closest kin.

SAMIN-DURR:70:13-14/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:70:13-14/r4.speaker: السوسي عن أبي عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:70:13-14/r4.claim: Al-Sūsī from Abū ʿAmr does not replace the hāʾ, since replacement would make the form heavier and substitution is meant to lighten speech.
SAMIN-DURR:70:13-14/r4.anchor: السوسي عن أبي عمرو قالوا: لأنه يؤدي إلى لفظ هو أثقل منه

SAMIN-DURR:70:13-14/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:70:13-14/r5.speaker: الزهري
SAMIN-DURR:70:13-14/r5.claim: Al-Zuhrī reads تؤويه and تنجيه with ḍamma on pronoun hāʾ, its original vowel.
SAMIN-DURR:70:13-14/r5.anchor: وقرأ الزهري " تؤويه " و " تنجيه " بضم هاء الكناية، وهو الأصل

ZAJJAJ:v5p220#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p220#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p220#2/r1.claim: Faṣīla is a person's closest clan or tribe.

ASAD-NOTES:70:5/r5.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:70:5/r5.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:70:5/r5.claim: The sinner would ransom himself with his children, spouse, brother, sheltering kin, and everyone else on earth.
ASAD-NOTES:70:5/r5.anchor: desire to ransom himself from suffering at the price of his own children

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p193/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p193/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p193/r1.claim: Al-Ma'arij lists children, spouse, brother, clan, then everyone on earth; Abasa lists brother, parents, spouse, and children.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p193/r1.anchor: وفي سورة المعارج على عكس ذلك، فقد بدأ بالأبناء، فالصاحبة فالأخ فالفصيلة، ثم انتهى بأهل الأرض أجمعين.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p193/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p193/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p193/r2.claim: Because Abasa describes fleeing, the order moves from more distant relatives toward those closest to a person; spouses and children are the most intimate.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p193/r2.anchor: المقام في (عبس) مقام الفرار والهرب، قال تعالى: {يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ المرء} والإنسان يفرّ من الأباعد أولاً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p195/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p195/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p195/r1.claim: Because the person facing punishment is a criminal desperate to escape, he would sacrifice even his closest loved ones and, in principle, all people for himself.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p195/r1.anchor: والمجرمُ مستعدٌّ لِفعْلِ أيِّ شيء لينجو ولو أن يبدأ بأقرب المُقَرَّبين إليه وأحبهم إلى قلبه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p195/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p195/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p195/r2.claim: The sequence begins with children because the preceding verse has already mentioned close kin, then expands to more distant people and finally everyone on earth.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p195/r2.anchor: جرى ذِكْرُ القرابات قبل هذا المشهد فقال: {وَلاَ يَسْأَلُ حَمِيمٌ حَمِيماً}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p195/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p195/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p195/r3.claim: The following description of human anxiety and panic explains why the criminal starts by offering those nearest and dearest to him.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p195/r3.anchor: ذكر بعد هذه الآيات أن الإنسان {خُلِقَ هَلُوعاً * إِذَا مَسَّهُ الشر جَزُوعاً * وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ الخير مَنُوعاً}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p195/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p195/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p195/r4.claim: Starting with the closest relatives shows that the punishment is beyond imagining and leaves no room for bargaining.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p195/r4.anchor: يدل على أن العذاب فوق التصور، وهولُهُ أبعدُ من الخيال بحيث جعله يبدأ بأقرب الناس إليه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p195/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p195/r5.speaker: أنوار التنزيل
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p195/r5.claim: Anwār al-Tanzīl explains that each criminal becomes so absorbed in himself that he wishes to ransom himself with his nearest and dearest, rather than care about their welfare.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p195/r5.anchor: جاء في (أنوار التنزيل) في قوله تعالى: {يَوَدُ المجرم لَوْ يَفْتَدِي مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمِئِذٍ بِبَنِيهِ}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p195/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p195/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p195/r6.claim: The ransom list proceeds through children, wife, brother, clan, and all earth’s people, leaving no one except the person seeking ransom.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p195/r6.anchor: فرتَّبهن ترتيباً آخر مبتدئاً بالأبناء فالزوجة فالأخ فالفصيلة، وفيهم الأبوان ثم انتهى بأهل الأرض أجمعين، فلا يبقى أحد غيره

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p912/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p912/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p912/r1.claim: Ma'arij depicts the sinner wishing to ransom himself from punishment with his sons, spouse, brother, clan, and everyone on earth; the scene is one of attempted ransom.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p912/r1.anchor: أما في سورة المعارج فالمشهد مشهد فِداء وذَكَر القرابات

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p912/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p912/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p912/r3.claim: The passage omits parents because God commanded kindness to them and they have an exalted status; the author says one might flee from them, but could not ransom oneself by consigning them to Hell.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p912/r3.anchor: لم يذكر في الآية الافتداء بالأم أو الأب لأن الله تعالى أمر بالإحسان إليهما ودلّ على عظيم مكانة الأبوين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p692/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p692/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p692/r1.claim: In the flight scene, a person flees from those furthest from his heart toward those closest; when offering ransom, he starts with the dearest and moves outward, hence the different orders in Abasa and Al Maarij.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p692/r1.anchor: في سورة عبس المشهد هو مشهد الفرار يخلو المرء بنفسه ويفر المرء أولا من الأبعد إلى الأقرب إلى قلبه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p692/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p692/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p692/r2.claim: The ransom list omits mother and father because God commanded that parents be honored, so a person may not ransom them from punishment.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p692/r2.anchor: والملاحظ أنه في حالة الفداء هذه لم يذكر الأم والأب وهذا لأن الله تعالى أمر بإكرام الأب والأم ويمنع الإفتداء بالأم أو الأب من العذاب إكراماً لهما

NASHR:v1p471/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p471/r1.speaker: صاحب الكافي وصاحب التبصرة
NASHR:v1p471/r1.claim: For hamza in tuʾwīhi and ruʾyan, al-Kāfī and al-Tabṣira prefer replacing it with a matching wāw or yāʾ without assimilation; al-Tabṣira says this is the established practice.
NASHR:v1p471/r1.anchor: ورجح الإظهار صاحب " الكافي "، وصاحب " التبصرة " وقال: إنه الذي عليه العمل

NASHR:v1p471/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p471/r2.speaker: صاحب التذكرة والداني
NASHR:v1p471/r2.claim: Al-Tadhkira and al-Dānī prefer replacement followed by assimilation, citing its explicit transmission from Hamza and agreement with the rasm; al-ʿUnwān likewise gives only this form.
NASHR:v1p471/r2.anchor: ورجح الإدغام صاحب " التذكرة " والداني في " جامع البيان " فقال: هو أولى ; لأنه قد جاء منصوصا عن حمزة، ولموافقة الرسم

NASHR:v1p471/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p471/r3.speaker: صاحب التيسير
NASHR:v1p471/r3.claim: Al-Taysīr gives the two treatments equally, and al-Shāṭibī follows that presentation.
NASHR:v1p471/r3.anchor: وأطلق صاحب " التيسير " الوجهين على السواء، وتبعه على ذلك الشاطبي

NASHR:v1p471/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p471/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p471/r6.claim: For ruʾyā wherever it occurs, readers agree to replace the quiescent hamza with wāw after ḍamma.
NASHR:v1p471/r6.anchor: فأجمعوا على إبدال الهمزة منه واوا لسكونها وضم ما قبلها

NASHR:v1p471/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p471/r7.speaker: الهذلي
NASHR:v1p471/r7.claim: Al-Hudhali, al-Dānī, and others allow Abū Jaʿfar's assimilation of the wāw into the following yāʾ; Ibn Shurayḥ also reports it but weakens it.
NASHR:v1p471/r7.anchor: فأجازه أبو القاسم الهذلي، والحافظ أبو عمرو، وغيرهما، وسووا بينه وبين الإظهار

NASHR:v1p471/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p471/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p471/r8.claim: Although assimilation agrees with the rasm, the author prefers clear articulation as more analogical and the practice of most reciters; deletion based only on rasm is impermissible.
NASHR:v1p471/r8.anchor: فإن الإظهار أولى وأقيس، وعليه أكثر أهل الأداء، وحكي فيه وجه ثالث

QIRAAT-ER:70:13:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:70:13:4#1/r1.speaker: hmz
QIRAAT-ER:70:13:4#1/r1.claim: Hamza easing removes the glottal stop in tuʾwīhi and lengthens the vowel; the source says the change is phonological and leaves meaning unchanged.
QIRAAT-ER:70:13:4#1/r1.anchor: hmz, mutawatir: Hamza removal: glottal stop of tuʾwīhi simplified to long vowel

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p318#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p318#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p318#3/r1.claim: Qatāda glosses a person's “faṣīla” as his tribe.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p318#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وفصيلته التي تؤويه ﴾ قال قبيلته

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p318#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p318#3/r2.speaker: معمر
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p318#3/r2.claim: Maʿmar says he had heard that a person's “faṣīla” means the mother who nursed him.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p318#3/r2.anchor: قال معمر وبلغني أن فصيلته أمه التى أرضعته

ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#2/r1.claim: Faṣīla means the nearest clan from whom a person separated; Al-Ālūsī prefers this to al-Rāghib’s “clan separated from him.”
ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#2/r1.anchor: أي عشيرته الأقريبن الذين فصل عنهم كما ذكره غير واحد ولعله أولى من قول الراغب عشيرته المنفصلة عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#2/r2.speaker: ثعلب
ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#2/r2.claim: Thaʿlab defines faṣīla as a person’s closest forefathers.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#2/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#2/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda defines faṣīla as the clan branch, or thigh subdivision.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#2/r4.claim: The clan shelters him through his affiliation with it, and he seeks refuge in it during calamities.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#2/r4.anchor: أي تضمنه انتماء إليها أولياذا بها في النوائب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r10.claim: Faṣīlah is his clan, the people from whom he branched.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r10.anchor: {وأخيه وفصيلته} عشيرته التي فصل منهم. وقال مجاهد: قبيلته.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r11.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r11.claim: Mujahid glosses faṣīlah as his tribe.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r12.speaker: غيره
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r12.claim: Other commentators understand it as his closest relatives.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r13.claim: The clan is the group that embraces and shelters him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r13.anchor: التي تؤويه} أي التي تضمه ويأوي إليها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r1.claim: His faṣīla is the clan from whom he separated.

BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r2.claim: His clan shelters him through kinship or in times of hardship.
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r2.anchor: تضمه في النسب أو عند الشدائد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r11.claim: “Faṣīla” is his clan, those nearest from whom he separated; they are the closest remaining relatives.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r11.anchor: أي عشيرته الذين هم أقرب من فصل عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r12.claim: His clan shelters and protects him in hardship, so it has the greatest claim on him and is dearest to him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r12.anchor: تضمه إليها عند الشدائد وتحميه , لأنه أقرب الناس إليها وأعزهم عليها فهم أعظم الناس حقا عليه وأعزهم لديه

DURR-FULL:v8p280/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p280/r13.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p280/r13.claim: Qatada says the criminal will wish to ransom himself with his dearest loved ones, then his progressively nearer relatives, because of that Day’s severity.
DURR-FULL:v8p280/r13.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {ولا يسأل حميم حميما} قال: شغل كل إنسان بنفسه عن الناس {يبصرونهم}

DURR-FULL:v8p281/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p281/r2.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v8p281/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses fasīla as a man’s clan.
DURR-FULL:v8p281/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك رضي الله عنه {وفصيلته} قال: عشيرته

DURR-FULL:v8p281/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p281/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v8p281/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says fasīla refers to the tribe to which a person belongs.
DURR-FULL:v8p281/r3.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب رضي الله عنه {وفصيلته التي تؤويه} قال: قبيلته التي ينتسب إليها

DURR-FULL:v8p281/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p281/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p281/r4.claim: Mujahid likewise glosses fasīla as the tribe.
DURR-FULL:v8p281/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {وفصيلته} قال: قبيلته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361#4/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361#4/r1.anchor: وفصيلته قال ابن قتيبة أي عشيرته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361#4/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361#4/r2.claim: It means his nearest tribal kin.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361#4/r2.anchor: وقال الزجاج هي أدنى قبيلته منه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361#4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361#4/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361#4/r3.claim: Tuʾwīhi means that his kin shelter and embrace him.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361#4/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361#4/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361#4/r4.claim: He would wish to ransom himself with these relatives and the other things mentioned.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225/r1.claim: The sinner wishes to ransom himself from punishment with his children, spouse, brother, sheltering clan, or everyone on earth—even all its wealth or his dearest child—but no ransom will be accepted.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225/r1.anchor: أي: لا يقبل منه فداء ولو جاء بأهل الأرض، وبأعز ما يجده من المال، ولو بملء الأرض ذهبا،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225/r2.speaker: مجاهد والسدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225/r2.claim: Mujahid and al-Suddi explain faṣīla as a person's tribe and clan.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225/r3.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225/r3.claim: ʿIkrima explains faṣīla as the particular branch or subdivision from which a person comes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225/r3.anchor: وقال عكرمة: فخذه الذي هو منهم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225/r4.speaker: مالك عن أشهب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225/r4.claim: Ashhab reports Malik's gloss of faṣīla as the man's mother.

JISHUMI:v10p7077/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7077/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7077/r13.claim: Faṣīla is a subgroup separated from its tribe by descent from an ancestor; the root means cutting.
JISHUMI:v10p7077/r13.anchor: والفصيلة: الجماعة المنقطعة عن جملة القبيلة برجوعها إلى أب خاص، وأصل الفصل: القطع.

JISHUMI:v10p7078/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7078/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7078/r18.claim: The sinner wishes to ransom himself by giving his sons, wife, brother, sheltering kin, and everyone on earth to the fire.
JISHUMI:v10p7078/r18.anchor: يود المجرم أي: يتمنى المشرك والمذنب لو يفتدي من عذاب يومئذ ببنيه

JISHUMI:v10p7078/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7078/r20.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7078/r20.claim: Faṣīla is also closest kin who shelter him and to whom he turns for shelter.
JISHUMI:v10p7078/r20.anchor: وقيل: بنوه وفصيلته قيل: عشيرته الأقربون منه التي تؤويه يأوون إليه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r12.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd understands fasīla as the clan that supports a person.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r12.anchor: أحدهما : عشيرته التي تنصره , قاله ابن زيد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r13.speaker: مالك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r13.claim: Malik understands fasīla as the mother who raises him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r13.anchor: الثاني : أنها أمه التي تربيه , قاله مالك , وقال أبو عبيدة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r14.speaker: أبو عبيدة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r14.claim: Abu Ubayda says fasīla is a rank below the tribe.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r14.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة : الفصيلة دون القبيلة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r15.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r15.claim: Al-Dahhak says the clan is where a person turns by lineage.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r15.anchor: أحدهما : التي يأوي إليها في نسبه , قاله الضحاك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r16.claim: Alternatively, it is where a person seeks refuge when afraid.

MUQATIL:70:8-18/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:70:8-18/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:70:8-18/r8.claim: His faṣīla is his clan and nearest kin group, to whom he turns for shelter.
MUQATIL:70:8-18/r8.anchor: { وفصيلته التي تؤويه } [آية: 13] يعني رهطه وفخذه الأدنى الذي يأوي إليهم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#4/r1.claim: His clan means his closest relatives, who shelter him through kinship.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#4/r1.anchor: وعشيرته الادنين ﴿ التي تؤويه ﴾ تضمه انتماء اليها

QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r11.claim: The listed loved ones are his sons, wife, brother, and faction; his fasila is his clan.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r11.anchor: ثم ذكرهم فقال: { ببنيه. وصاحبته } وزوجته. { وأخيه. وفصيلته } أي عشيرته

QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r12.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r12.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Zayd explain the fasila as the clan that supports a man.

QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r13.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r13.claim: Malik says the fasila is a man's mother, who raises him; al-Mawardi transmits this from him through Ashhab.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r13.anchor: وقال مالك: أمه التي تربيه. حكاه الماوردي ورواه عنه أشهب

QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r14.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r14.claim: Abu Ubayda defines the fasila as a kin group below the tribe.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r14.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: الفصيلة دون القبيلة

QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r15.speaker: ثعلب
QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r15.claim: Thaʿlab defines a man's fasila as his nearest fathers.

QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r16.speaker: المبرد
QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r16.claim: Al-Mubarrad says fasila means a piece of the body, a smaller unit than a tribe.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r16.anchor: وقال المبرد: الفصيلة القطعة من أعضاء الجسد، وهي دون القبيلة

QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r17.claim: A man's ʿitra is called his fasila by analogy with a part of his body.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r17.anchor: وسميت عترة الرجل فصيلته تشبيها بالبعض منه.

QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r18.claim: For an endowment or bequest to one's fasila, the general reading means the clan, while the narrow reading means nearest forefathers; the general sense is more common in speech.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r18.anchor: وهنا مسألة، وهي: إذا حبس على فصيلته أو أوصى لها فمن ادعى العموم حمله على العشيرة

QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r19.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r19.claim: Taʾwīhi means to gather him in and protect him from fear if he is afraid.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:11-14/r19.anchor: ومعنى: «تؤويه» تضمه وتؤمنه من خوف إن كان به.
